name: KBQA end-to-end: public benchmark questions answered from Wikidata slices through SymbolicLM, KnowledgeLinker and the reference route
registered_by: kbqa-eval-agent (owner direction of 2026-10-01: KBQA is the project's yardstick from now on)
kind: evaluation-only (CPU/auto-device SymbolicLM parse; no training; omp LLM baselines on subscriptions)
frozen_before_results: Written before the first chain answer was scored. Harness, scorer and attribution rules (tools/eval/kbqa/) were written first and checked on 3 hand-made questions only. Later changes to the scorer or to the mechanical Wikidata-to-circuits mapping (tools/eval/kbqa/memory.mjs) are recorded as deviations with the stage at which they happened; a rerun after a component change (linker M0, world-v1) is a new tagged run, never a replacement of the old numbers.

system_under_test.chain: question (message only) -> SymbolicLM service (lib/symbolic-lm, auto-device parse lock) -> Agent (server/agent.mjs: admission, KnowledgeLinker sop/linking.mjs + sop/copula-linker.mjs over the lexicon of the session's base memory, reference route) -> result packet
system_under_test.memory: one SQLite base memory per suite and stage, `kbqa-<suite>-<stage>`, imports core-min, in a private chat data root (datasets_sources/kbqa/chat_data, gitignored). Built mechanically from the Wikidata slice of the stage's questions (tools/eval/kbqa/slice.mjs, memory.mjs): the question entities, the gold answer entities, their one-hop neighbourhood with distractors, the incoming statements for the annotated properties, a second hop towards the answers, labels and aliases. No per-question authoring; lexicon forms come only from Wikidata property labels and aliases.
system_under_test.slice_is_gold_guided: The slice contains the facts about the gold answer entities by construction, so the evaluation measures the chain GIVEN the knowledge; the scorer reports separately when the slice cannot contain the answer. It is not a claim about open retrieval.
system_under_test.isolation: every question runs in its own conversation on a fresh clone of the base memory; reads do not reinforce (policy.reinforce false).

suites.mintaka: Mintaka test (Amazon Science, CC-BY-4.0), 1000 rows stratified over 9 complexity types, gold from the benchmark
suites.lcquad2: LC-QuAD 2.0 test (CC-BY-4.0 per the figshare record), up to 1000 rows stratified by query structure; gold = the benchmark's SPARQL executed on query.wikidata.org at build time (rows whose gold is empty are dropped and counted in meta.json)
suites.simplequestions: SimpleQuestions-Wikidata answerable test (CC-BY-3.0), 1000 rows; gold by SPARQL; any gold value is correct (the benchmark asks for one)
suites.qald10: QALD-10 test, all 393 English questions (MIT licence of the repository), gold from the benchmark
suites.sealing: eval/suites/kbqa-<name>/test.jsonl are sealed test exports (AGENTS.md direction 9): only tools/eval/kbqa/ reads them, no generator or training code does. The questions are public, new test material: no model was trained on them by us.

hypotheses.H1: The chain's strict accuracy is low on all four suites at this stage (below 25% at the 300-question stage), because the mechanical lexicon lacks verb lemmas and the KnowledgeLinker has no converse frames. This is a baseline to be improved, not a target.
hypotheses.H2: The chain's wrong-answer rate (a definite answer that differs from the gold) is below 10% on every suite: failures are overwhelmingly honest unknowns or clarifications.
hypotheses.H3: On the simple questions (SimpleQuestions, simple types of the other suites) the grok llm-agent baseline reading the same facts as text is more accurate than the chain; the paired difference has a 95% bootstrap interval above 0.
hypotheses.H4: The largest failure layer of the chain is the KnowledgeLinker (relation unknown), not the memory slice or the engine.

metrics.primary: accuracy = correct / n over the stage (correct, wrong, unknown are exclusive; wrong = a definite answer that differs from the gold; a gold no answered by unknown is unknown)
secondary: failure attribution by layer (symbolic_lm, linker, memory_slice, engine, with sub-classes)
metrics.intervals: Wilson 95% for proportions; paired bootstrap (4000 resamples) for chain-versus-baseline and rerun-versus-rerun differences over the shared questions

stopping_rules.stages: 100, then 300, then all, per suite; the interval is computed after each stage
stopping_rules.broken: stop the suite and report if more than 20% of the first 100 questions end in an error or an empty SOP
stopping_rules.futility: do not run the full set when the 95% Wilson upper bound of the accuracy at 300 is below 3% (a conclusion different from 'the chain does not answer this suite yet' is excluded)
stopping_rules.decisive: stages 100 and 300 are always run (cheap, local); the full run continues unless broken or futile
stopping_rules.record: every stop is recorded with its stage, numbers and reason in the journal, the topic notes (topic kbqa), the experiment record and the report

baselines.llm-agent: omp (skills/omp-run, read/write/edit tools only, fenced folders under datasets_sources/kbqa-baseline/) with Grok (xai-oauth/grok-4.20-0309-reasoning) as the main baseline and 2-3 parallel GLM (zai) sessions; each reads the statements of the slice about its questions as text and answers from them only. Reported on the first 100 questions per suite; GLM numbers are added when they finish and never block the main numbers.

reruns: After linker-m0-agent logs done (per-session lexicon, KnowledgeLinker) and when world-v1 exists, the stages are rerun with tag `m0`; the report shows both runs and the paired difference.
